gap: No result ChatGPT got says how many hours of driving fit in each camera's built-in memory before the oldest footage is overwritten. With front and rear recording, the 70mai M800 holds about 7.3 h in its 128 GB, the REDTIGER F77 about 4.6 h in its 128 GB, and the DDPAI Z90 Master about 2.0 h in its 64 GB. Each figure comes from reviewer-measured bitrates.
standout_why: From the results ChatGPT got, I read the DashCamTalk reviewer pages and the 70mai.com M800 spec page. The 70mai.com page lists 128 GB of eMMC and 4K/1080p resolution, but gives no recording time and no bitrate. I could not open the cited 70mai.store M500 page, the DDPAI Z90 Master page or the F77 store page: they returned HTTP 429 or DNS errors, and the manuals.plus M800 PDF would not parse. So I could not confirm by reading that those pages leave out a recording time. A search snippet suggests DDPAI's own page claims '3.5h' for 4K front and rear on the eMMC. If so, that rival has part of this for one product only. None of the results gives a comparison across products, and none works the time out from measured bitrates.
decides: This supports ChatGPT's pick of the 70mai M800 for front and rear recording. Its smaller 1080p rear stream (8.19 Mb/s) lets 128 GB hold roughly 1.6 times the loop time of the dual-4K F77. The DDPAI Z90 Master's 64 GB eMMC holds only about 2 h at its measured bitrates. That makes its microSD slot a necessity, not a nice extra, for anyone who wants 'built-in memory' to be enough.

findings.label: Built-in storage and resolution
findings.note: Maker spec page, which reads 'Built-in eMMC Storage'. It lists no bitrate and no recording time.

findings.label: Measured video bitrate
findings.note: Measured by Augustus: 2160p HEVC 30fps HDR front, 1080p HEVC HDR rear, about 265 MB per one-minute 4K clip, 128 GB formatted FAT32. DashCamTalk's spec card lists 29.4 / 10.1 Mbps instead.

findings.label: Hours of front + rear loop footage in the built-in memory (derived)
findings.note: 128 GB × 8,000 Mbit/GB ÷ 39.09 Mb/s ÷ 3,600 s/h = 7.3 h. This uses the nominal capacity, so it is an upper bound because some space is reserved. Front only: 1,024,000 ÷ 30.9 ÷ 3,600 = 9.2 h.

findings.label: Measured bitrate and usable eMMC space
findings.value: front ≈31,000 kbps + rear ≈24,000 kbps = 55 Mb/s; 114 GB usable of 128 GB
findings.source_title: REDTIGER F77 Version 1 (128GB) Review and Impressions – DashCamTalk, DT MI, 2025-08-02
findings.note: The reviewer, DT MI, states that 'about 4.1 hours of combined front and rear video can be expected'. They also report that REDTIGER's website claims 8 hours for the 128 GB version and say this is 'reasonably accurate for single channel recording'. A 256 GB version exists, but the reviewer gave no figures for it.

findings.label: Hours of front + rear loop footage in the built-in memory (derived)
findings.source_title: REDTIGER F77 Version 1 (128GB) Review and Impressions – DashCamTalk
findings.note: 114 GB × 8,000 Mbit/GB ÷ 55 Mb/s ÷ 3,600 = 4.6 h. The reviewer's 4.1 h figure is lower and they don't show their arithmetic. Front only: 912,000 ÷ 31 ÷ 3,600 = 8.2 h, which matches REDTIGER's 8 h claim.

findings.label: Measured bitrate and storage
findings.value: front 42.1 + rear 30.1 + interior 17.8 Mbps; 64 GB built-in eMMC + microSD up to 512 GB
findings.note: The same page contradicts itself: the intro says 64 GB eMMC and the Strengths list says 32 GB. Forum posts reportedly mention 128 GB in retail units (model DZ003), but I did not open them. I used 64 GB, the capacity ChatGPT's card stated.

findings.label: Hours of loop footage in the built-in eMMC alone (derived)
findings.value: ≈2.0 h front + rear; ≈1.6 h with all three channels
findings.note: Front + rear: 64 × 8,000 ÷ 72.2 Mb/s ÷ 3,600 = 1.97 h. Three channels: 512,000 ÷ 90.0 Mb/s ÷ 3,600 = 1.58 h. These are upper bounds based on nominal capacity.

DDPAI's own eMMC recording-time claim, which a search snippet gives as '3.5h' for 4K front and rear. ddpai.com/en-us/products/z90-master and ddpai.com/dash-cams/z90-series/ both returned HTTP 429 on every try, so I left the claim out.
